# Syphrone

> Syphrone is a privacy-first, browser-based cryptographic platform providing AES-256-GCM message
> encryption, steganography, RSA-2048 key generation, and multiple cipher tools — all running 100%
> client-side with zero server-side data transmission.

## Entity Information

- **Canonical name**: Syphrone
- **Canonical URL**: https://syphrone.netlify.app/
- **Type**: Security Web Application / Cryptographic Platform
- **Status**: Free, publicly accessible
- **Developer**: Armaan Sunasara
- **Role**: Co-founder & Full Stack Developer
- **Organisation**: Techyboy (https://techyboy.live)
- **First published**: 2026
- **Last updated**: 2026-08-20

## What Syphrone Does

Syphrone helps users protect text messages using browser-based cryptography. All operations execute
inside the user's browser using the Web Crypto API. No plaintext, keys, or ciphertext ever leave the
device to any Syphrone server.

## Tools & Features

- **AES-256-GCM Encryption** — Symmetric encryption using the Web Crypto API with PBKDF2 key derivation (310,000 iterations, SHA-256).
- **RSA-2048 Key Generator** — Generates asymmetric key pairs in-browser.
- **PNG Steganography** — Hides messages inside image pixel data without visual distortion.
- **Zero-Width Unicode Cipher** — Encodes messages in invisible Unicode characters.
- **Morse Code Encoder/Decoder** — Converts text to and from Morse code.
- **DNA Code Cipher** — Encodes text using nucleotide sequences.
- **Emoji Cipher** — Maps characters to emoji sequences.
- **Binary & Hex Encoding** — Standard encoding utilities.
- **Secure Vault** — Local encrypted storage of messages using AES-GCM.
- **Command Palette** — Keyboard-accessible tool launcher (Ctrl+K).
- **Decoy Mode** — Disguises the interface to protect against shoulder-surfing.
- **Screen Shield** — Blurs content on window blur events.
- **Theme System** — 20 visual themes (10 free, 10 premium).
- **PWA / Install Support** — Installable as a Progressive Web App on Android and desktop.

## Security Model

- Encryption algorithm: AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption with associated data — AEAD).
- Key derivation: PBKDF2 with 310,000 iterations, SHA-256 digest, random 16-byte salt.
- Nonce: Random 12-byte IV generated per encryption operation.
- Randomness source: Web Crypto API `crypto.getRandomValues()`.
- 100% client-side: no server, no database, zero backend, and no user accounts or sign-ins.
- No analytics script or telemetry captures plaintext, keys, or ciphertext.
- Fully open and free to use for everyone with zero login barriers.

## Privacy Commitment

Syphrone is designed as a zero-knowledge, zero-backend tool. User plaintext and keys are processed
entirely in local memory and are never transmitted. No backend, Firebase authentication, or remote
tracking is used.

## What Syphrone Is Not

- Not a VPN or network-level privacy tool.
- Not a secure messaging protocol (no end-to-end transport layer).
- Not a password manager.
- Not independently security-audited (as of 2026-08-20).
- Does not protect against device-level threats, keyloggers, or screen capture.

## Canonical Questions & Answers

**What is Syphrone?**
Syphrone is a browser-based cryptographic platform for encrypting messages and hiding them using
steganography. All processing is client-side.

**Who made Syphrone?**
Syphrone was built by Armaan Sunasara, co-founder of Techyboy (techyboy.live).

**What encryption does Syphrone use?**
AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2 key derivation (310,000 iterations). The algorithm runs in-browser via the
Web Crypto API.

**Does Syphrone store my data?**
No. Core encryption operations run entirely in-browser. No plaintext, key, or ciphertext is sent to
any Syphrone server.

**Is Syphrone free?**
Yes. All cryptographic tools and all 20 signal themes are completely free and open for everyone.

**What is steganography in Syphrone?**
Syphrone's steganography tool hides secret messages inside PNG image pixel data. The result is a
visually identical image that contains an embedded hidden message.

**Does Syphrone work offline?**
Yes. Once installed as a PWA, the core tools function offline.

- PBKDF2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveKey#pbkdf2
- OWASP Top 10:2025: https://owasp.org/Top10/2025/en/
